extracted.intended_audience: Independent Organ Procurement Organizations (IOPOs), Histocompatibility Laboratories (HCLs), transplant hospitals, Medicare providers, CMS officials, legal counsel, and other stakeholders commenting on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory changes and procedural requirements governing contractor hearing officer decisions, CMS reviewing official review, and discretionary Administrator review for reimbursement appeals involving IOPOs and HCLs, including thresholds, timelines, submission content, and effects of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor notice and NPR appealability
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 42 CFR 405.1801(a)(1) and (2), and 405.1803, the contractor must give the provider written notice of the contractor determination for the cost period in a notice of the total amount of program reimbursement (NPR). The NPR is an appealable determination, subject to the jurisdictional and other requirements of the statute and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPR triggers appeal rights; contractors must provide written notice of total program reimbursement amounts as the basis for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount in controversy threshold for IOPOs and HCLs
rubrics_metrics.description: 42 CFR 413.420(g) provides that an IOPO or a Histocompatibility Laboratory (HCL) that is dissatisfied with a Medicare contractor's cost report determination may request a hearing before a contractor hearing officer if the amount in controversy is $1,000 or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule would explicitly tie 405.1811(a)(2) and 405.1811(c)(3) to 42 CFR 413.420(g) to confirm the $1,000 threshold applies to IOPOs and HCLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to a contractor hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: An IOPO or HCL dissatisfied with a contractor's cost report determination may request a hearing before a contractor hearing officer in accordance with 42 CFR 405.1811 through 405.1833 when the amount in controversy meets the required threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and requirements for requesting and obtaining a contractor hearing are governed by the cited provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS reviewing official review availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the contractor hearing officer decision is issued, an IOPO or HCL is entitled to obtain review by a CMS reviewing official (see 42 CFR 405.1801(b), 405.1833, 405.1834(b) and (c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CMS reviewing official reviews final contractor hearing officer decisions and issues a written decision; proposed changes clarify the reviewing official's role and the possibility of subsequent Administrator review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator discretionary review authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator has discretionary authority to review CMS reviewing official decisions and contractor hearing officer decisions for reimbursement appeals for IOPOs and HCLs, including the ability to take own-motion review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule codifies that the Administrator may grant or deny review at his/her discretion, may review on his/her own motion, and may issue a final decision binding the Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Administrator review (405.1801(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to 405.1801(a) to state that Administrator review means review provided for in section 1878(f) of the Act (42 U.S.C. 1395oo(f)) and 42 CFR 405.1875 and 405.1834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies cross-references and aligns the definition with the proposed procedures in 405.1834.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final agency decision cross-reference (405.1803(d)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to 405.1803(d)(1)(ii) to reflect that a final agency decision by the Administrator is as described in 405.1875(e)(4) and 405.1834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures regulatory text reflects Administrator review provisions in 405.1834.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount in controversy cross-reference in 405.1811
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to 405.1811(a)(2) and 405.1811(c)(3) to specify that IOPOs and HCLs are subject to an amount in controversy as set forth in 42 CFR 413.420(g) (i.e., $1,000 or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the established $1,000 threshold governs right to a contractor hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of contractor hearing decision on extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions to 405.1813(e) to reflect that a contractor hearing decision denying an extension request and dismissing the appeal is final and binding on the provider, unless reviewed by a CMS reviewing official in accordance with 405.1834(b)(2)(i), or the Administrator, or reopened and revised by contractor hearing officer(s) in accordance with 405.1885 through 405.1889.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions granting extensions are not subject to immediate review but may be examined during later reviews; contractor hearing officer must promptly send decisions to the appropriate CMS component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor hearing officer must send decisions to CMS component (405.1813(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision specifying that the contractor hearing officer(s) promptly sends the decision to the appropriate component of CMS (currently the Center for Medicare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures CMS components receive the administrative record and decisions to facilitate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final jurisdictional findings and dismissal reviewability
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions to 405.1814(a)(5) and 405.1814(c)(3) to reflect that final jurisdictional findings and jurisdictional dismissal decisions by the contractor hearing officer(s) are subject to the CMS reviewing official procedure in accordance with 405.1814(d) and 405.1834(b)(2)(i) and (ii), and the possibility of review by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional dismissal decisions are final and binding unless reviewed by a CMS reviewing official, subsequently reviewed by the Administrator, or reopened and revised in accordance with 405.1885-405.1889.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on further administrative review of jurisdictional findings (405.1814(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision stating any finding by the contractor hearing officer as to whether he or she has jurisdiction to grant a hearing on a specific matter is not subject to further administrative review, except as provided in 405.1814(d); such findings may be reviewed solely during the course of a CMS reviewing official review of specified contractor hearing officer decisions or during Administrator review of a CMS reviewing official decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrows routine collateral attack of jurisdictional findings while preserving review through the specified review channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewability of discovery/disclosure rulings (405.1821(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to specify that to the extent a ruling authorizes discovery or disclosure of a matter for which an objection based on privilege or other protection (case preparation, confidentiality, undue burden) was made before the contractor hearing officer(s), that portion of the ruling may immediately be reviewed by a CMS reviewing official or the Administrator in accordance with 405.1834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also proposes staying proceedings upon notice of intent to seek immediate review and related conforming editorial changes removing 'the Administrator through the.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of contractor hearing officer's decision (405.1833)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendment adding paragraphs to reflect that a contractor hearing officer's decision issued in accordance with 405.1831 is final and binding on all parties and on the contractor, unless the decision is reviewed by a CMS reviewing official, reviewed by a CMS reviewing official and then by the Administrator, or reopened and revised by the contractor hearing officer(s) in accordance with 405.1885 through 405.1889.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also adds paragraph specifying final contractor hearing decisions are subject to the provisions of 405.1803(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and sequence of reviews (405.1834(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision that CMS or a provider party dissatisfied with a final contractor hearing officer decision, upon submitting a request that meets 405.1834(c), is entitled to further administrative review by a CMS reviewing official; the decision may then be subject to discretionary review by a designated CMS reviewing official and by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the reviewing official considers whether the contractor hearing officer decision is consistent with controlling legal authority (405.1834(e)(1)) and the evidence in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for CMS reviewing official to exercise review (405.1834(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to specify the CMS reviewing official exercises review authority in response to a request from a provider party that meets 405.1834(c), in response to a request from CMS, or may exercise discretion to take own motion review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes provider-initiated, CMS-initiated, and own-motion review as bases for the reviewing official's action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to forward decisions and records to CMS component (405.1834(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision requiring contractor hearing officer(s) to promptly send copies of any decision specified in 405.1834(b)(2) or (3), or in 405.1821(d)(2) and the underlying administrative record to the appropriate component of CMS (currently the Center for Medicare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires the appropriate CMS component to examine each such decision, along with review requests and submissions, to assist the CMS reviewing official's and Administrator's exercise of review authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction to provider request timing and content (405.1834(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed correction changing 'or' to 'and' so that a provider's request for review by a CMS reviewing official is granted only if (i) the date of receipt by the appropriate CMS component of the review request is no later than 60 days after the provider received the contractor hearing officer decision, and (ii) the request seeks review of a decision listed in 405.1834(b)(2), and the provider complies with 405.1834(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that both timing and substantive compliance requirements must be met for the request to be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate review timing for discovery/disclosure rulings (405.1834(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to specify that a request from a party or CMS for immediate review of a contractor hearing officer ruling authorizing discovery or disclosure must be made as soon as practicable after the ruling is made, but in no event later than 5 business days after the date the requesting party or CMS received notice of the ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a short, strict deadline for seeking immediate review of such rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Own-motion review procedures and Administrator trigger (405.1834(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed reorganization to state 'Own motion review of a CMS reviewing official.' The CMS reviewing official has discretion to take own motion review of a contractor hearing decision or other reviewable action. If the CMS reviewing official does not notify parties and the contractor that he or she intends to review within 90 days after the contractor hearing officer's decision, the Administrator may issue a notice instructing the CMS reviewing official to review the decision and issue a decision if the reviewing official fails to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator must provide copies of such notice to parties and CMS component; after receipt the CMS reviewing official must allow parties a reasonable period to comment on the issues identified by the Administrator. If no party requests review and the CMS reviewing official does not take review within specified time periods, the contractor hearing officer decision is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing official written decision content and distribution (405.1834(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of review, the CMS reviewing official issues a written decision that includes findings of fact and conclusions of law on jurisdictional issues and on the merits of each issue under review; and affirms, reverses, or modifies the contractor hearing decision or remands it to the contractor hearing officer for further proceedings. A copy must be sent promptly to each party, to the contractor, and to the appropriate component of CMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures reasoned written decisions and prompt distribution to interested parties and CMS components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and finality of CMS reviewing official decisions (405.1834(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision specifying that a decision of affirmation, reversal, or modification by the CMS reviewing official is final and binding on each party and the contractor except as set forth in 405.1834(g). The CMS reviewing official's decision may be reopened and revised in accordance with 405.1885 through 405.1889. A decision remanding an appeal to the contractor hearing officer(s) is not a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies finality, reopening authority, and distinguishes remands from final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to forward reviewing official decisions to Administrator (405.1834(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed addition specifying the CMS reviewing official must promptly send copies of the CMS reviewing official decision, along with any other submissions made by a party or CMS, to the appropriate component of CMS and to the Administrator c/o the CMS Office of the Attorney Advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an explicit transmission requirement to support potential Administrator review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request Administrator review (405.1834(g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed new paragraph specifying that CMS or any party to a CMS reviewing official decision may request Administrator review of a CMS reviewing official decision; no other provider, individual, or entity may request review. The Administrator may grant or deny review at his or her discretion and may also review any decision on his or her own motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the universe of eligible requestors to CMS and parties to the reviewing official decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content of Administrator review requests (405.1834(g)(2) and (g)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed specification that a party or CMS may request Administrator review of a CMS reviewing official decision within 15 days of their receipt. All requests and submissions must be sent to the Office of the Attorney Advisor, be in writing, attach a copy of the CMS reviewing official decision, and include a brief description of: those aspects of the decision with which the requestor is dissatisfied; the reasons; any argument or record evidence supporting its position; and any additional extra-record evidence along with a demonstration that such evidence was improperly excluded in proceedings (as described in 405.1823).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a short filing window and detailed content requirements to support Administrator consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator notice timing and contents (405.1834(g)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that the Administrator must issue a Notice advising parties of his or her intent to review or to decline to review within 30 days of receipt of a request for review. The Notice must be sent to the parties, the contractor, and the appropriate CMS component. A Notice to review must contain a brief statement of the issues under review and solicit comments; a Notice declining review need not provide the basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures prompt notification and an opportunity to comment if review is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Administrator non-response within 30 days (405.1834(g)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed specification that if the Administrator declines to review the reviewing official decision or does not issue a determination regarding review within 30 days of receipt of a request to review, the decision of the CMS reviewing official is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a time-based lapse rule making the reviewing official decision final if Administrator does not act within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator own-motion review timing (405.1834(g)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed specification that within 45 days of Administrator's receipt of a CMS reviewing official's decision, the Administrator may issue a Notice of Review on his or her own motion. The Notice must be sent to parties, contractor, and appropriate CMS component and contain issues under review and solicit comments. If Administrator does not issue a determination regarding own-motion review within 45 days, the reviewing official decision is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a 45-day window for Administrator to initiate own-motion review or the reviewing official decision becomes final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator proceedings and finality (405.1834(g)(4) and (g)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Administrator elects to review, the Administrator will set deadlines for comments; the Administrator's decision affirming, reversing, or modifying the CMS reviewing official's decision is final and binding on each party and the contractor. If Administrator does not issue a written decision that affirms, reverses, modifies or remands within 60 days of issuance of the Notice of Review, the CMS reviewing official's decision becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator decisions are final; remands are explicitly non-final; time limits (60 days) constrain Administrator action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator remand requirements (405.1834(g)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed specification that the Administrator may remand the CMS reviewing official's decision to the CMS reviewing official, to the contractor hearing officer, or to the contractor. A remand must vacate the CMS reviewing official's and/or contractor hearing officer decisions as to the specific issues remanded; be governed by the same criteria that apply to remands by the Administrator to the Board under 405.1875(f)(2); require the entity to which the matter is remanded to take specific actions on remand; and result in issuance of a new decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets substantive and procedural expectations for remands to ensure corrective action and issuance of a new decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming changes to 413.420(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed conforming revisions to 413.420(g) to reflect that if the amount in controversy is $1,000 or more, any IOPO or histocompatibility laboratory that disagrees with a contractor's cost determination is entitled to a contractor hearing, review by a CMS reviewing official, and discretionary Administrator review of a CMS reviewing official decision in accordance with 405.1801(b)(2) and 405.1811 through 405.1834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns appeals provisions in 413.420(g) with the proposed changes to the administrative review ladder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date applicability to pending and timely-filed appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule would apply to administrative appeals timely filed with a contractor hearing officer on or after the effective date, and/or appeals pending before a contractor hearing officer or a CMS reviewing official on the effective date. For good cause extensions under 405.1813, IOPOs and HCLs that have not filed timely and wish to seek an extension have an additional 60 days after the effective date to seek an extension without meeting the 'reasonable time' requirements of 405.1813 (but must meet all other requirements of that section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transitional relief and specifies which appeals and extension requests the rule applies to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening and revision authority (405.1885-405.1889 cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several provisions refer to the contractor hearing officer's and CMS reviewing official's decisions being reopenable and revisable in accordance with 405.1885 through 405.1889.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates an existing statutory/regulatory mechanism for reopening decisions is preserved as part of the review architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and review assistance by appropriate CMS component
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that the appropriate CMS component examines each contractor hearing officer decision that is reviewable under 405.1834(b)(2) or (3), or 405.1821(d)(2), along with any review requests and submissions, in order to assist the CMS reviewing official's and the Administrator's exercise of review authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures internal CMS components play an active role in preparing issues and materials to facilitate higher-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections to organ/transplant cost rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed technical corrections: change 'kidney' to 'organ' in 412.116(c); clarify 413.404(b)(3)(ii)(A) definition of deceased donor SAC to reference 'organ acquisition'; and add registry fees to allowable costs for deceased donor SAC at 413.404(b)(3)(ii)(C)(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are textual/corrective edits intended to align regulatory language with prior intent and to include registry fees previously omitted.
